title: 'The West Wing' live debate at 20: 'The perfect episode for the perfect show at the perfect time' - NewsBreak
text:
By Debra Birnbaum ,
6 hours ago Kennedy-Nixon. Lincoln-Douglas. And Santos-Vinick. 'KPop Demon Hunters 2' planned for 2029 release on Netflix: Everything to know Surely the presidential debate that aired live on NBC 20 years ago, on Nov. 6, 2005, as an episode of The West Wing — deserves to be included among the list of the best political face-offs ever, at least among fans of the hit drama. The hour-long installment featured Jimmy Smits’ Democratic candidate Matthew Santos going head-to-head with Alan Alda ’s Republican party nominee Arnold Vinick live twice , for the East Coast and the West Coast. As scripted by Lawrence O’Donnell , then an executive producer for the show, the men agreed to throw away the pre-negotiated rules and dive deep into issues ranging from immigration to gun control to Medicare. Nearly 10 million viewers tuned in — a significant bump over the series’ average at the time. “It was the perfect episode for the perfect show at the perfect time,” says director Alex Graves , now an executive producer for The Diplomat .
